specification.title: A migration whose reversal deletes its marker
steps: Runner A applies { m1 }. m1 inserts marker m1.
Revert with the framework's default selection. m1's reversal deletes marker m1.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the revert has returned and the reapply has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: If a revert reports a migration as reverted, its history entry is absent and its marker is absent.

execution.description: ActiveRecord::Base.transaction on the connection pool. Pool size is the case pool_max. A nested transaction(requires_new: true) is a savepoint named active_record_N. create! writes the markers. MigrationContext applies and rolls back files under a temporary path. No full Rails application, no database.yml, and no callback is registered on the scored path.

configuration.pool: connection pool size from the case pool_max
configuration.faults: category C and D faults are injected on PG::Connection before Active Record sees the error

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

knowledge: A reported revert says the migration's effects are gone. The next apply is what shows that history and the database agree: the migration runs again.

api_outcome.contract: ActiveRecord::MigrationContext runs migrations from files. On PostgreSQL the migration and its schema_migrations change share a transaction unless disable_ddl_transaction is set. Migrator#with_advisory_lock calls PostgreSQLAdapter#get_advisory_lock, which is pg_try_advisory_lock. A second process that does not get the lock raises ActiveRecord::ConcurrentMigrationError instead of waiting. https://api.rubyonrails.org/v8.1.4/classes/ActiveRecord/Migration.html
